svg.title: Bar chart. MRSTFT, 1,000 held-out clips from 929 songs; lower is better. No processing, the dry stems, unchanged: 1.17; Best published encoder, as released, best of four: StemFX, AFx-Rep, FX-Encoder++, RelFX; frozen, small readout on top: 0.869; StemFX design, retrained on our data, our data and recipe: 0.485; FX-Encoder++ design, retrained on our data, our data and recipe: 0.463; Our baseline, ViT-Tiny; all settings from one learned summary token; second run 0.504: 0.492; Baseline + conv first layer, convolutions before the ViT; alone, within run-to-run noise: 0.495; Baseline + slot readout, one query per stem and effect: 0.439; Both changes (FX-JEPA), conv first layer + slot readout: 0.413. Below it, a table of every model we scored: StemFX, released weights, frozen 0.869; AFx-Rep, released weights, frozen 0.893; FX-Encoder++, released weights, frozen 0.897; RelFX, released weights, frozen 1.024; StemFX design (CNN), trained on our data 0.485; FX-Encoder++ design, trained on our data 0.463; Our baseline (ViT) 0.492; Our baseline + slot readout 0.439; FX-JEPA: conv first layer + slot readout (best) 0.413. Run-to-run noise bounds are about 6% for the baseline family and 12% for the best model (98.75% bootstrap bounds over songs; the observed second-run gaps are 2.4% and 7.3%). Spectral only; no listening test.
